title: Client Bridge: Pagination Resumption, Streaming Fallbacks, and Cross-Language Compatibility PRD
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem statement: We need a unified client contract for paginated fetches and streaming responses across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs that minimizes application-level complexity, supports resumable consumption for intermittent networks, and degrades gracefully when older clients or servers are present. This PRD defines surface-level requirements, acceptance criteria, migration constraints, and rollout steps for SDK and runtime changes to support: opaque cursor pagination, cursor-resumption semantics, streaming chunk framing with resumable tokens, negotiated fallbacks, and explicit compatibility guarantees.
scope: In scope: standardizing cursor semantics (opaque tokens), server-side sequence numbers for stream resumption, client support libraries in Python/TS/Go exposing: iterate_pages(), fetch_page(cursor), stream_events(resume_token), and higher-level helpers for idempotent retry and backoff. Out of scope: full redesign of server APIs (we assume compatibility shims) and changing existing public endpoints that are not paginated/streaming.
non_goals: This ticket does not change embedding APIs, does not introduce new authentication models, and will not add new datastore-level guarantees. We will not force application-level changes beyond using the new client helpers.
requirements: 1) Pagination: server returns an opaque cursor string plus minimal metadata (total_estimate optional). Clients must treat cursor as opaque and only pass it back to the server. SDKs expose a lazy iterator that yields items or pages.
2) Resumable pagination: server may include an optional expiry TTL and a stable fallback offset for large/backfill operations. Client should persist cursor if caller requests resume semantics.

3) Streaming: streaming endpoints must emit chunk frames with sequence numbers and an optional resume_token checkpoint. SDKs provide two consumer patterns: pull-based async iterator and callback-based consumer for TS/Go; Python supports both sync generator and async generator variants.

4) Retry semantics: clients must implement safe retries for idempotent list/fetch operations using exponential backoff with jitter. For non-idempotent endpoints, SDK surface should require explicit idempotency token parameter.
5) Backpressure & windowing: streaming helpers must expose a consumer-configurable window size and buffer limit. Default window size = 10 messages; default buffer limit = 4MB.

6) Compatibility: runtime will advertise stream/pagination feature version via header 'X-Redwood-Client-Feature' and negotiate fallbacks. SDKs must detect older servers and automatically switch to non-resumable streaming or offset pagination with a clear warning in logs.
7) Telemetry: each SDK must emit usage signals for pagination/resume/stream-fallback events to the console pipeline (tokenized, no PII).
8) API ergonomics: provide minimal surface for common flows: iterate_all_items(), iterate_pages(page_size), start_stream(on_message, on_error, resume_token=None).
acceptance_criteria: Automated interop tests: For each language (Python/TS/Go) the interop suite validates: basic pagination, resume-from-cursor, resume-after-network-failure for streams, and negotiated fallback when server advertises older feature-version.

Behavioral tests: client must be able to resume a streaming session within the server-provided TTL without data duplication beyond allowed dedup window. Integration tests assert no more than 1 duplicate per item under resume conditions.
Performance: paginated fetch (page_size=50) 95th percentile latency < 180ms in the canary environment. Streaming resume latency (time to resume and receive next message) 95th percentile < 350ms.
SDK ergonomics: library exposes documented helpers with examples in README and sample apps for each language. API signatures accept both sync and async/await patterns where idiomatic.

Backward compatibility: clients detect older servers and invoke fallback flows without throwing exceptions; unit tests cover detection and fallback path. No existing customers on supported SDKs should see breaking exceptions during the 90-day deprecation window.
Security: feature negotiation does not expose sensitive IDs; security review sign-off obtained for header/token semantics.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary runtime + SDK alpha): deploy runtime with feature flag 'client_bridge_v1' in us-west-2 to internal canary tenants; publish alpha SDK packages to internal registry for Python/TS/Go. Collect interop metrics for 2 weeks.

Phase 2 (expanded beta): publish public beta SDKs, enable feature for 10% of traffic with automatic rollback on regressions. Provide migration guide and lint rule for customers to detect cursor persistence patterns.
Phase 3 (general availability): flip feature flag to 100% after 4 weeks of stable metrics, publish GA SDKs and stabilization notes. Begin 90-day deprecation timer for legacy behavior endpoints.
Phase 4 (post-GA): remove legacy-only code paths in SDKs after 90 days, release minor versions with breaking-change migration notes if necessary.
compatibility_matrix: Python SDK: support 3.8+, recommend 3.10+. New helpers added in client v2.4.0; patch adapters available for v2.2.x with reduced ergonomics.
TypeScript SDK: support Node 16+. New async iterator surface in 1.8.0; backwards shim uses callback API when server feature is absent.
Go SDK: support 1.20+. Streaming resume helpers added in 0.12.0; older 0.x clients will continue to work but require explicit resume token handling by caller.
Runtime: supports feature-version header negotiation values v1 and v1-alpha. Older runtimes without negotiation return HTTP 426 with guidance header for clients.
Console/Monitoring: rollout dashboards will show per-language resume_success_rate and fallback_rate.
Deprecation: servers older than runtime-2024.11 will be eligible for deprecation; customers will be notified via 90-day email cadence.
performance_targets: Paginated list (page=50): p95 < 180ms in canary; p99 < 400ms targeting production baseline.
Stream resume: time-to-first-message after resume token < 350ms p95.
Memory: default SDK buffer should not exceed 4MB for page/stream consumer under normal load; documented knob to increase for high-memory environments.
Error rates: client-side unrecoverable failures in interop tests must be < 0.5% during beta.
decision_log: 2025-01-20: Chose opaque cursor model (server-provided) over offset-driven pagination to keep server flexibility. Agreed to include optional stable offset in metadata for migration/backfills.

2025-01-28: Streaming resume will use (sequence_number, resume_token) tuple to limit duplication and simplify verification on resume. Sequence_number is incremental per stream and enforced by runtime.
2025-01-31: Default retry/backoff policy: exponential backoff base=200ms, max=8s, full jitter. Clients expose retry parameters but use safe defaults.
2025-02-02: Compatibility negotiation will use 'X-Redwood-Client-Feature' request header and 'X-Redwood-Feature-Status' response header with values 'v1','v1-alpha' or 'legacy'.
